record.paper_title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Extending Chebyshev and Klee function results to Hilbert and Banach spaces
record.original_question: Within the finite-dimensional Euclidean framework X = R^n for Chebyshev functions and Klee functions, results concern single-valuedness, characterizations, and Chebyshev-point behavior for proper lower semicontinuous functions. How can those results be extended to Hilbert spaces, or even to general Banach spaces?

evidence.quote: Chebyshev set and Klee set problems can be generalized to problems involving functions.
Facts 7.5 and 7.7 below concern Chebyshev functions and Klee functions; see [37] for proofs.
Problem 8. How do the results on Chebyshev functions and Klee functions extend to Hilbert spaces or even general Banach spaces?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space (in particular, a Hilbert space) and let $f:X	o(-\infty,+\infty]$ be a Legendre function in the sense of Bauschke–Borwein–Combettes; i.e., $f$ is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, essentially smooth, and essentially strictly convex, with $\mathrm{int}\,\mathrm{dom}\,f
eq\emptyset$. The Bregman distance induced by $f$ is
$$D_f(x,y) := f(x) - f(y) - \langle 
abla f(y), x-yangle, \qquad x\in\mathrm{dom}\,f,\ y\in\mathrm{int}\,\mathrm{dom}\,f.$$

Given a proper lower semicontinuous function $\varphi:X	o(-\infty,+\infty]$, define the associated Chebyshev function and Klee function (with respect to $D_f$) by
$$C_\varphi(x) := \inf_{y\in X} igl\{\varphi(y) + D_f(x,y) igr\}, \qquad K_\varphi(x) := \sup_{y\in X} igl\{D_f(x,y) - \varphi(y) igr\},$$
and call a point $y^\star$ realizing the infimum (respectively supremum) a Chebyshev point (respectively Klee point) of $\varphi$ at $x$.

In the finite-dimensional Euclidean setting $X=\mathbb{R}^n$, the following types of results are known for such $\varphi$:

(i) characterizations of when $C_\varphi$ and $K_\varphi$ are single-valued (i.e., the corresponding Chebyshev/Klee point is unique) in terms of convexity-like properties of $\varphi$;

(ii) representations and regularity (e.g., continuity, differentiability) of the Chebyshev and Klee functions;

(iii) characterizations of $\varphi$ via the behavior of its Chebyshev points and Klee points (for instance, that uniqueness of Klee points everywhere forces $\varphi$ to be, up to standard transformations, convex).

Problem. Extend these single-valuedness results, regularity properties, and Chebyshev/Klee-point characterizations for proper lower semicontinuous functions $\varphi$ with respect to the Bregman distance $D_f$ from the finite-dimensional Euclidean setting to:
(a) infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces $X$, and
(b) general real Banach spaces $X$,
identifying the geometric and analytic hypotheses on $X$ and on the Legendre function $f$ under which each of the finite-dimensional results continues to hold.
artifact.status_search_result: Several follow-up works extend Chebyshev set, Klee set and Chebyshev center results with respect to Bregman distances from $\mathbb{R}^n$ to Banach space settings (e.g., works on Bregman distance, approximate compactness and convexity of Chebyshev sets in Banach spaces; Klee sets in Banach spaces for the right Bregman distance; and results without the coercive condition). However, the full extension of the Chebyshev-function and Klee-function results (single-valuedness, characterizations, Chebyshev-point behavior for proper lsc $\varphi$) to Hilbert and general Banach spaces appears to remain only partially addressed.
